headline: Semis Led Friday's Rally — Now Markets Brace for a Fresh Week
body_html:
Wall Street enters Monday's session carrying momentum from a broadly positive Friday close. Of 544 names tracked in our universe, 364 finished higher against 174 decliners — a lopsided result that put Semiconductors at the top of the sector table with a gain of 4.18%. Industrials and Materials also closed in the green, adding 1.33% and 1.16% respectively, while Energy contributed a modest 0.83% advance. The session's lone meaningful laggards were Homebuilders, off 0.73%, and Software, which slipped a fractional 0.08%.

The boldest single-name moves came from the chip space. MaxLinear surged nearly 15% and Synaptics added 14.08%, while Allegro MicroSystems tacked on 8.66% — together reinforcing Semiconductors' commanding lead. On the downside, Western Digital and Seagate Technology each fell roughly 10%, a synchronized selloff in the storage segment that stood in stark contrast to the rest of the tech landscape. Freight carrier RXO Inc and advanced-materials specialist Materion each jumped above 9%, signalling appetite beyond pure technology.

Heading into Monday's open, traders will be parsing geopolitical headlines that emerged over the weekend — including reports of fire and smoke near an Aramco facility in Riyadh and an alleged plot uncovered in the UK — for any read-through to energy and risk sentiment. Several market watchers have flagged this week as a moment to reassess cash positions. Watch pre-market futures and early tape action in Semiconductors and Storage for the clearest signal on whether Friday's optimism carries over.

briefs.headline: Storage Stocks Stumble Into the Weekend
briefs.body: Western Digital and Seagate Technology each dropped more than 10% on Friday, making the storage segment the session's clearest weak spot even as the broader technology complex rallied. Traders will be watching whether that pressure persists when Monday's session opens or whether bargain hunters step in.

briefs.headline: Fire Reported Near Saudi Aramco Facility in Riyadh
briefs.body: Reuters reported that witnesses observed fire and smoke in the vicinity of an Aramco installation in Riyadh over the weekend. The incident adds a fresh layer of uncertainty to energy markets heading into Monday's open, coming at a time when geopolitical risk has already been elevated across the Middle East.

briefs.headline: OpenAI Safety Departure Raises Governance Questions
briefs.body: An OpenAI employee focused on safety has resigned and publicly called for oversight measures analogous to nuclear-level safeguards on artificial-intelligence development. The departure intensifies scrutiny of how frontier AI labs balance rapid product development against risk management, a debate that increasingly resonates with institutional investors in the sector.

briefs.headline: Some Investors See Dip as a Buying Opportunity
briefs.body: Despite pockets of volatility, at least one market commentary making the rounds this weekend argues that the recent weakness has created an opening to put sidelined cash to work. The note points to specific areas of the market seen as oversold, a thesis that could drive selective buying pressure early in Monday's session.

briefs.headline: Portugal Probe Into US Use of Lajes Base Adds to Geopolitical Noise
briefs.body: Portuguese prosecutors are examining whether American military use of the Lajes Air Base in the Azores in connection with operations against Iran was lawful, according to Reuters. The inquiry is an early-stage legal matter but adds to the constellation of geopolitical developments that traders must weigh as the new week begins.

briefs.headline: Private Capital Accelerates Its Push Into Hollywood
briefs.body: A growing body of evidence points to private capital firms reshaping how major film and television projects are financed and produced, moving beyond traditional studio structures. The shift has implications for media-sector valuations and may attract fresh attention from investors looking for alternative avenues as public-market volatility continues.
